claims.quote: Jenkins was back among them soon, remarking that she was making twenty knots already.
claims.description: A navy destroyer capable of sustained high speeds (twenty knots at the start, later forty knots), speculative for the era's vessels.

claims.quote: but all night they charged along at forty knots, with lights extinguished
claims.description: A destroyer sustaining forty knots for hours, far beyond the speed of 1898 warships.

claims.quote: the engine-room staff nursed the oil feed and the turbines. Black smoke—unconsumed carbon that even the blowers could not ignite—belched up from the four short funnels
claims.description: An oil-fired turbine-driven naval destroyer, a propulsion arrangement not yet in service in 1898.

claims.quote: Then they turned on both searchlights, and saw buoys ahead, to starboard and port.
claims.description: Powerful searchlights on a small warship used for navigating channels at night.

claims.quote: "They've found that sentry," he said, "and have telephoned Fort Independence; but it's no good.
claims.description: Coastal forts alerted by telephone to a prison escape and stolen warship.
Ship-board wireless radio operators and wireless sets used to intercept naval and shore messages across the coast and Atlantic.

claims.quote: "The air's full o' talk," he said. "Casey's at the receiver, still listening, but I made out only a few words like 'Charleston,' 'Brooklyn,' 'jail,' 'pirates,' 'Pensacola,' and one phrasing 'Send in pursuit.'"
claims.description: Wireless broadcast traffic between naval stations and ships that can be overheard to learn of pursuit.

claims.quote: Jenkins looked to the north, just in time to see a tongue of red dart from a casemate port; then, as the bark of the gun came down the wind, a spurt of water lifted from the sea about a hundred yards ahead.
claims.description: A battleship with heavy casemated guns firing on and pursuing a stolen destroyer in the open Atlantic.

claims.quote: Every nation in the world would send its cruisers after them, and no civilized country would receive them.
claims.description: A coordinated international naval manhunt for escaped naval prisoners with a stolen destroyer.

claims.quote: "There is not a craft in the world that can catch her," rejoined Jenkins
claims.description: A destroyer so fast that no other vessel in the world can overtake it.

claims.quote: Denman, in view of future need of it, took upon himself the winding of the chronometers; and the days went on, Casey and Munson reporting messages sent from shore to ship; battle-ships, cruisers, scouts, and destroyers appearing and disappearing, and their craft racing around the Atlantic like a hunted fox.
claims.description: Prolonged transatlantic naval pursuit guided by wireless messages from shore to ships.

claims.quote: Gripping his legs tightly around the body of Jenkins, he sagged down and pressed the tips of his forefingers into two vulnerable parts of the thick neck, where certain important nerves approach the surface
claims.description: A jujutsu nerve-pressure technique that disables a large man, leaving him unable to speak or move.

claims.quote: Oh, you're all right, Captain Jenkins," said Denman. "You'll breathe easier to-morrow, and in a week, perhaps, you may speak in a whisper
claims.description: Prediction that the disabled man will recover breathing within a day and regain speech only in a week.

claims.quote: But you will not reach the coast. You will be hunted down and caught before then.
claims.description: Denman predicts the escapees will be hunted down and captured before reaching Africa.
